accepted.question_text: Let an arrangement be a pair (L, P) in the Euclidean plane where L is a finite set of straight construction lines and P is a finite set of registration marks such that every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L, and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P. For a given integer k >= 0 representing the number of registration marks, what are the possible lower and upper bounds on the number of construction lines that an arrangement with exactly k registration marks can determine?

evidence.quote: Suppose k >= 0 number of points are given in the plane. How many construction lines k points must determine?
In this paper, empirical evidence is reported for small numbers of k offering partial answers to the three problems above.

accepted.question_text: Let an arrangement be a pair (L, P) in the Euclidean plane where L is a finite set of straight construction lines and P is a finite set of registration marks such that every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L, and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P. If |P| = k, and two construction lines have the same slope exactly when they are parallel, how many distinct slopes or directions can the construction lines of such an arrangement determine as a function of k?

evidence.quote: How many distinct slopes, or directions, are defined by construction lines that k points determine?
In this paper, empirical evidence is reported for small numbers of k offering partial answers to the three problems above.

accepted.question_text: Let an arrangement be a pair (L, P) in the Euclidean plane where L is a finite set of straight construction lines and P is a finite set of registration marks such that every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L, and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P. For a given integer k >= 0, how many projectively or combinatorially distinct sets of construction lines can partition the plane while meeting in exactly k registration marks?

evidence.quote: How many distinct sets of construction lines partition the plane, such that the lines meet at exactly k points?
The first two problems are problems about bounds. The third problem is an enumeration problem.

accepted.question_text: Given an arrangement (L, P) of construction lines and registration marks in the Euclidean plane, where every point in P is the intersection of at least two lines in L and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P, which such arrangements also satisfy the additional linear-space condition that every pair of distinct points in P lies on some line of L? Equivalently, which arrangements of this kind form a finite linear space?

evidence.quote: Which arrangements of construction lines and registration marks satisfy this assumption? Put in another way, which arrangements form a (finite) linear space?
I have not been able to identify other arrangements containing shapes that define linear spaces (i.e., in which any two distinct points lie on a line).

accepted.question_text: For arrangements (L, P) of construction lines and registration marks in the Euclidean plane with k >= 3 registration marks, can any valid arrangement determine more than k + 1 construction lines while still obeying the rules that every point of P is an intersection of at least two lines in L and every two nonparallel lines in L intersect in a unique point of P? Equivalently, is it true that every such arrangement has at most k + 1 construction lines?

evidence.quote: It is reasonable to ask then, are there any arrangements containing shapes with k registration marks such that they determine greater than k + 1 construction lines?
We conjecture that such arrangements do not exist: Conjecture 1. At most k + 1 construction lines are determined by k >= 3 registration marks in the plane.
